title: Sprint 4 - Files, Data Processing and Error Handling
description: Learn how Python applications work with real-world data. Build a Developer Data Import System that reads and writes files, processes CSV and JSON data, validates records, handles malformed input, and uses exceptions to prevent application failures.

tickets.title: Read a Text File
tickets.description: The development team stores project notes in a text file. Read the contents of `project_notes.txt` and display them in the terminal.
tasks: Create or use the file `project_notes.txt`.
Open the file using Python.
Read the complete contents of the file.
Print the contents to the terminal.
Ensure the file is properly closed after reading.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program and verifies that the complete file contents are read and displayed correctly.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong file name.
Opening the file in write mode instead of read mode.
Reading only the first line.
Forgetting to close the file.
hints: Use `open()` with read mode.
The `read()` method can retrieve the complete file contents.

solution.main.py:
with open("project_notes.txt", "r") as file:
    content = file.read()

print(content)

tickets.title: Process File Lines
tickets.description: The project notes file contains one task per line. Read the file and count how many non-empty task lines it contains.
tasks: Read all lines from `project_notes.txt`.
Process the file line by line.
Ignore empty lines.
Count the remaining lines.
Print the result using the format `Total tasks: <value>`.
learning_objectives: Learn how to process files line by line.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program against test files containing different numbers of lines and verifies the calculated count.
common_mistakes: Counting empty lines.
Reading the entire file and incorrectly counting newline characters.
Forgetting to remove whitespace before checking whether a line is empty.
hints: A file object can be iterated over using a `for` loop.
Use `strip()` to remove surrounding whitespace.

test_cases.input:
Fix login
Add tests

Update README

tickets.title: Write a Project Report
tickets.description: The application needs to generate a summary report for the development team. Create a Python program that writes the generated report to `project_report.txt`.
tasks: Create a report containing the project name, total tasks, and completed tasks.
Open `project_report.txt` in write mode.
Write the report to the file.
Run the program and verify that the file contains the expected information.
learning_objectives: Learn the difference between read and write modes.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program and verifies that `project_report.txt` contains the expected report.
common_mistakes: Opening the file in read mode.
Writing the wrong information.
Appending when the task requires replacing the existing report.
hints: Use write mode when creating or replacing the contents of a file.
Use `write()` to place text into the file.

scoring_rules.expected_output:
Project: YCode
Total tasks: 10
Completed tasks: 7

solution.main.py:
report = "Project: YCode\nTotal tasks: 10\nCompleted tasks: 7"

with open("project_report.txt", "w") as file:
    file.write(report)

tickets.title: Read Developer Data from JSON
tickets.description: Developer information is now stored in a JSON file named `developers.json`. Read the JSON file and convert its contents into Python data.
tasks: Open `developers.json`.
Load the JSON data using Python's JSON library.
Access the developer records.
Print the name of each developer.
learning_objectives: Learn how to use Python's `json` module.
Convert JSON data into Python dictionaries and lists.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program with the provided JSON file and verifies that all developer names are correctly extracted.
common_mistakes: Treating JSON as plain text instead of parsing it.
Accessing dictionary values incorrectly.
Forgetting to import the `json` module.
hints: Python provides the `json` module for working with JSON.
Use `json.load()` when reading JSON directly from a file.

solution.main.py:
import json

with open("developers.json", "r") as file:
    developers = json.load(file)

for developer in developers:
    print(developer["name"])

tickets.title: Update Developer JSON Data
tickets.description: The system needs to add new developer information to the existing JSON data. Load the developer list, add a new developer, and save the updated data back to the JSON file.
tasks: Read the existing `developers.json` file.
Create a new developer record containing `name`, `role`, and `active` fields.
Add the new developer to the existing list.
Write the updated list back to `developers.json`.
Ensure the existing developer records are preserved.
learning_objectives: Read and modify structured JSON data.
Convert Python objects back into JSON.
Understand the difference between loading and dumping JSON.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program and verifies that the new developer is added without removing or modifying existing records.
common_mistakes: Overwriting the existing developer list before loading it.
Writing Python dictionary syntax that is not valid JSON.
Forgetting to save the modified data.
hints: Load the existing list before modifying it.
Use `json.dump()` to write Python data back to a JSON file.

test_cases.expected_result: Existing developers remain and the new developer is present

solution.main.py:
import json

with open("developers.json", "r") as file:
    developers = json.load(file)

new_developer = {
    "name": "Sneha",
    "role": "Frontend Developer",
    "active": True
}

developers.append(new_developer)

with open("developers.json", "w") as file:
    json.dump(developers, file, indent=2)

tickets.title: Import Developer Data from CSV
tickets.description: The company receives developer information as CSV files. Read `developers.csv` and convert each row into a Python dictionary.
tasks: Open `developers.csv`.
Read the CSV using Python's `csv` module.
Treat the first row as the column headers.
Convert each developer row into a dictionary.
Print each developer's name and role.
learning_objectives: Learn how to use Python's `csv` module.
Convert tabular data into Python dictionaries.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program against the provided CSV file and verifies that all records are read correctly.
common_mistakes: Manually splitting CSV lines without considering the CSV format.
Treating the header as a developer record.
Accessing columns using incorrect names.
hints: Python provides `csv.DictReader` for CSV files with headers.
Each row returned by `DictReader` behaves like a dictionary.

scoring_rules.expected_output:
Rahul - Backend Developer
Priya - Data Scientist
Arun - DevOps Engineer

solution.main.py:
import csv

with open("developers.csv", "r") as file:
    reader = csv.DictReader(file)

    for developer in reader:
        print(f"{developer['name']} - {developer['role']}")

tickets.title: Validate Developer Records
tickets.description: Imported developer data cannot be trusted because external files may contain incomplete records. Validate each developer record before processing it.
tasks: Require every developer record to contain `name`, `role`, and `active`.
Treat records with missing required fields as invalid.
Separate valid and invalid records.
Count the number of valid records.
Count the number of invalid records.
learning_objectives: Learn how to check required fields.
Process valid and invalid records separately.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the validation logic against valid and malformed records and verifies the resulting counts.
common_mistakes: Assuming every record contains all required fields.
Accessing missing dictionary keys directly and crashing.
Counting invalid records as valid.
hints: Use dictionary methods such as `get()` when a key may not exist.
Validate the record before processing its values.

tickets.title: Handle Invalid Input
tickets.description: The developer import utility currently crashes when a user enters an invalid numeric value. Update the application so invalid input is handled gracefully.
tasks: Ask the user to enter the number of years of experience.
Convert the input to an integer.
Handle cases where the user enters non-numeric text.
Print `Invalid experience` when conversion fails.
Print the entered experience when conversion succeeds.
learning_objectives: Handle invalid user input without crashing the application.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program with both valid numeric input and invalid text and verifies that both cases are handled correctly.
common_mistakes: Not catching `ValueError`.
Using a broad exception without understanding the expected error.
Allowing the program to terminate when invalid input is provided.
hints: Converting invalid text to an integer raises `ValueError`.
Place the conversion inside a `try` block.

tickets.title: Handle Missing Files
tickets.description: The import utility currently crashes when the expected data file does not exist. Update the application to handle missing files gracefully.
tasks: Attempt to read `developers.json`.
Handle the case where the file does not exist.
Print `Developer data file not found` when the file is missing.
Continue without crashing the application.
tickets.evaluation: Runs the program with an existing file and a missing file and verifies that both cases are handled correctly.
common_mistakes: Catching the wrong exception.
Printing an error but still trying to access unavailable data.
Using a broad `except` without handling the specific problem.
hints: Python raises `FileNotFoundError` when an expected file does not exist.
Handle the exception around the file-opening operation.

tickets.title: Build the Developer Data Import Pipeline
tickets.description: The company now needs a complete developer data import pipeline. Build a Python application that reads developer data, validates records, handles invalid input and missing files, and generates a clean JSON report containing only valid developer records.
tasks: Read developer records from `developers.csv`.
Convert CSV rows into Python dictionaries.
Validate that every record contains `name`, `role`, and `active`.
Separate valid and invalid records.
Count valid and invalid records.
Handle a missing input file without crashing.
Write valid records to `valid_developers.json`.
Generate `import_report.txt` containing the total, valid, and invalid record counts.
Ensure malformed records do not prevent valid records from being imported.
learning_objectives: Combine file handling, CSV processing, JSON processing, validation, loops, functions, and exception handling.
Generate useful output files from processed data.
tickets.evaluation: Runs automated scenarios using valid data, malformed records, empty files, and missing files. Verifies generated JSON output, report contents, record counts, and graceful error handling.
common_mistakes: Stopping the entire import when one record is invalid.
Failing to handle a missing input file.
Writing invalid records to the output JSON.
Incorrectly calculating valid and invalid record counts.
Overwriting valid records while processing later invalid records.
hints: Separate the pipeline into small functions.
Validate every record before adding it to the valid collection.
Use exception handling around operations that can fail.
Only write validated records to the output JSON.

test_cases.expected_result: Zero valid and zero invalid records
